observation.visible_scene: A low-angle view looking upward through a grove of tall, straight tree trunks (redwood-like) toward a bright sun breaking through the canopy near the top-center of the frame. The sun produces a strong starburst glare and a chain of lens-flare artifacts in the lower-center: a green ring containing a red dot, and a second green ring with a yellow-red dot just below it. The forest floor of dirt, pine needles and twigs fills the bottom edge, and sunlit foliage is visible between the trunks.
visible_changes: The overall composition is essentially static across the excerpt: the trunks, the sun's position, the starburst rays, and the two lens-flare rings remain at the same screen coordinates from the first to the last frame.
No object (tree, leaf, or flare) shows detectable translation, expansion, or deformation relative to the frame edges.
The bright sun glare and the circular flare artifacts persist continuously rather than appearing or disappearing.
Any change in brightness or shimmer of the background foliage is too slight to confirm as real motion; the scene reads as a fixed, held shot.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the camera later pans, tilts, or whether wind begins to move the canopy after this segment.
The full extent of the forest and what lies beyond the top and side crop boundaries.
Any cause of the glare (time of day, sun position) or whether the flare is a lens artifact versus a real light source.
uncertain_details: Possible sub-pixel camera drift or tiny flicker in the sun's intensity is not clearly resolvable between frames.
The slight softness of the right-side trunk may be focus or occlusion rather than motion.
It is unclear if the flare rings shift at all; they appear locked to the sun's screen position.
